findings.title: Keep newly requested reruns pending until their outcome is observed

The poller clears ciPending and only resumes inspection when ciKey changes. Because GraphQL fetches only 100 contexts, a rerun outside that page can finish without changing ciKey when another check keeps the rollup red. Its ledger outcome then remains rerunning forever. findings.failure_scenario: A PR has 101 checks. REST discovers and reruns a timed-out check outside the first 100 GraphQL contexts. It passes at the same SHA, but a visible check remains failed; subsequent polls never reconcile the successful rerun or record flake evidence.

findings.title: Persisted references to the removed provider can prevent daemon startup
findings.detail: Removing the provider leaves startup validators unchanged. RuntimePolicy revalidates persisted routing preferences and cells against the current catalog; Factory also throws for persisted runtime models whose provider is absent. Thus an otherwise valid pre-change database can prevent the daemon from starting. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {RuntimePolicy} from "./src/router/runtime-policy.ts"; import {MODELS,PROVIDERS} from "./src/router/catalog.ts"; const f=await Bun.file("test/fixtures/routing-identity.json").json(); const id=f.snapshot.providers.find(id=>!PROVIDERS.some(p=>p.id===id)); try {new RuntimePolicy({routingCells:()=>[],routingPrefer:()=>[id],routingHistory:()=>[]},{},MODEL
findings.failure_scenario: A database written before the change has an operator routing preference naming the removed provider, a routing cell naming its model, or a runtime model attached to that provider. Starting the new daemon throws before serving requests or resuming runs.

findings.title: Legacy eval resume is explicitly tested to fail
findings.detail: The new retired-provider case asserts HTTP 400 when resuming an interrupted historical eval. EvalRunner.resume passes the stored request through submit/validateRequest, which rejects its now-unknown model ID. This contradicts the requested preservation of resume behavior and also prevents a mixed-model eval from continuing work on still-supported targets. The integration test could not execute here because its imports encounter the incompatible Zod dependency; the rejection path and contrary assertion are explicit in the code.
findings.failure_scenario: An interrupted pre-change eval stores the removed model among its requested targets. Calling limitless eval resume or POST /api/evals/:id/resume rejects the entire eval with an unknown-model error.

Line callbacks store pieces of multiline credentials in failure excerpts.

findings.title: Credential suffixes survive cuts inside ANSI sequences
findings.detail: The fixed overlap assumes normalization removes every ANSI sequence. Failure excerpt collection retains unbounded bytes on very long output lines.

findings.title: Preserve blank lines before redacting multiline credentials
findings.detail: The process line splitter discards empty lines. Reassembling those callbacks cannot reconstruct a credential containing a blank line, so literal redaction misses it. The output tail is redacted correctly, but failures retains the credential's nonempty lines, which then reach storage, logs and prompts. Targeted command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/gate-output-review.test.ts"`. findings.title: Account for escaped credential lengths at runner cuts
findings.detail: Redaction now recognizes JSON-escaped credentials, but the truncation overlap uses only literal credential lengths. An escaped credential can be longer, leaving its suffix after the overlap is removed. Reproduced through runGates with JSON-escaped output and ANSI padding crossing the runner's 64,000-character cap. Targeted command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/gate-output-review.test.ts"`. Assertion output: `Expected to not contain: "tail-credential"`; the returned output still contained that suffix.

findings.detail: Removing the previous 8,000-character per-line cap makes retained diagnostics unbounded in bytes. The line-count limit now permits dozens of arbitrarily large strings, and subsequent observations join and redact the entire buffer. Untrusted gate output can exhaust daemon memory or stall its event loop. Targeted command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/gate-output-review.test.ts"`. Output: `retained diagnostic characters: 39000107; previous bound: 312000`; the bounded-buffer assertion failed.

The normalization test failed with Expected to not contain: "credential-421"; Received: "ecret-credential-421". findings.detail: runSandboxed recognizes its trusted startup token through onStdoutLine. Enabling streaming redaction changes that token before recognition when a credential matches part of it. gold.summary: An incomplete terminal escape consumes part of a credential before it can be matched.
Terminal-control stripping changes with chunk boundaries and loses state at the hold limit.

findings.title: Overlapping credential matches make the streaming buffer unbounded
findings.detail: The cut-adjustment loop repeatedly retreats across overlapping matches, potentially reaching the start of the entire pending buffer. With credential `aaaaaaaa` and repeated `a` output, nothing is emitted until the stream ends, so tailLimit does not bound retention. A mocked subprocess emitting sixteen 1 MiB chunks with tailLimit=100 retained 17,901,021 additional live heap bytes before ending, although the returned result was only 100 characters. Continued output can exhaust daemon memory and repeatedly rescan an increasingly large buffer.

findings.title: Interrupted preparation without gate events cannot resume
findings.detail: Worktree creation precedes baseline execution and prepare completion. A crash in that interval leaves a valid legacy worktree but neither evidence accepted by this migration. Registration is therefore skipped on resume. The new interrupted-prepare test supplies gate events and misses this interval. Reproducer command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-ltAE7y/claude-501/review-legacy-check.ts interrupted-prepare`. Output: `interrupted-prepare { worktree_provenance: null }`, followed by `AssertionError: null !== 'legacy'`.
findings.failure_scenario: Before the cutoff, the old daemon creates a linked worktree and crashes before baseline gates emit events. After upgrading, the running prepare stage has no completion timestamp or gate evidence, and resume fails with Missing trusted Git paths.

findings.title: Legacy local worktrees are registered against the wrong repository
findings.detail: Existing local worktrees can belong to the original source repository, as the surrounding code and existing compatibility test explicitly support. Resume always passes the modern bare-cache path, which may not exist and does not own these worktrees. Even passing the correct source .git directory fails legacy.ts's mandatory bare-repository assertion. Reproducer command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-ltAE7y/claude-501/review-legacy-check.ts local-source`. Output: `error: Unsafe worktree Git administration`, caused by the assertion at legacy.ts:47. This check uses real Git and registration code, isolating only the repository-lock dependency.
findings.failure_scenario: A pre-upgrade local run has a missing sidecar and a linked worktree owned by repo.localPath/.git. The migration marks it legacy, but resume looks in local-<repo-id>.git and rejects the intact worktree.

gold.summary: Arbitrary assertion text mentioning a timeout is classified as a transient CI failure.
Retry eligibility ignores security failures outside the selected error line.
A paused PR is not inspected again when main recovers without another PR change.
An accepted rerun with a lost response is never reconciled to its later result.

findings.title: Resume suppressed PR failures when main recovers
findings.detail: A main-red inspection clears ciPending. Subsequent unchanged PR observations never inspect main again, so its recovery cannot resume the suppressed rerun or needs-fix reaction. Command: bun test /private/tmp/lr-UWn1Tq/claude-501/ci-review.test.js. Output: After main recovery: {"reruns":0,"pending":false,"mainState":{"test":{"red":true,"episode":1}}}; assertion failed: Expected length: 1, Received length: 0.
findings.failure_scenario: PR and main both fail the test check. Main subsequently passes, while the PR SHA and failed check remain unchanged. The PR remains suppressed indefinitely.

findings.title: Reconcile reruns whose POST response was lost
findings.detail: Only rerunning rows are reconciled. A successful POST with a lost response, or a crash before finishCiFailure, leaves rerun_requested. A later same-SHA success is ignored; another failure can prematurely mark the request failed_again without checking its actual attempt. Command: bun test /private/tmp/lr-UWn1Tq/claude-501/ci-review.test.js. Output: After same-SHA pass: rerun_requested; assertion failed: Expected: "failed_then_passed", Received: "rerun_requested".
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts the rerun, the connection resets before its response arrives, and attempt 2 passes at the original SHA. The ledger never records the flake.

findings.title: Resolve completed reruns with skipped conclusions
findings.detail: Completed conclusions outside success and bad fall through without changing rerunning. A skipped rerun therefore keeps successful CI pending forever and causes repeated REST inspection. Command: bun test /private/tmp/lr-UWn1Tq/claude-501/ci-review.test.js. Output: After completed skipped rerun: {"completed":false,"outcome":"rerunning"}; assertion failed: Expected: true, Received: false.
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out job is rerun, but an attempt-dependent condition skips it on attempt 2. GitHub reports the job completed/skipped and the rollup SUCCESS; the ledger remains rerunning indefinitely.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: Playwright security failures can be automatically rerun
findings.detail: Security detection ignores Playwright failure headings such as `1) [chromium] › tests/security.spec.ts:10:1 › rejects unauthorized access`. In a generic job concluded timed_out, that evidence does not prevent recording the failure and rerunning the job. This violates the security-test exclusion. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probes.ts"` produced `observed rerun POSTs: 1 ledger rows: 1` and `FAIL Playwright security timeout never reruns ... 1 !== 0`.
findings.failure_scenario: A generic test job times out and its log contains a Playwright failure heading naming security.spec.ts; the step name is generic and there are no failure annotations.

findings.title: Indented Playwright timeout diagnostics are not classified as transient
findings.detail: The Playwright alternative is anchored without allowing leading whitespace. Standard reporter output such as `    Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.` therefore produces ci.needs_fix instead of a rerun. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probes.ts"` produced `observed rerun POSTs: 0 needs_fix items: 1` and `FAIL indented Playwright timeout is transient ... 0 !== 1`.
findings.failure_scenario: A GitHub Actions job concludes failure after a Playwright test timeout, with the timeout diagnostic indented in its downloaded log.

findings.title: Main-red alerts are deduplicated per check instead of per repository
findings.detail: Each failing check name receives a separate ci.main_red key. When test and lint fail on both main and a PR, two repository items are emitted, contrary to the requested single repository item. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probes.ts"` produced `observed ci.main_red items: 2` and `FAIL one main-red feed item per repository ... 2 !== 1`.
findings.failure_scenario: One repository has two checks failing on main and the same two checks failing on a factory PR.

findings.title: Main-red failures are omitted from the failure ledger
findings.detail: The main-red branch continues before job inspection and recordCiFailure, so these PR failure signatures, SHAs, runner images, and outcomes are never persisted. Pausing reactions should not discard the requested failure history. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probes.ts"` produced `observed main-red ledger rows: 0` and `FAIL main-red PR failures enter the ledger ... 0 !== 1`.
findings.failure_scenario: A non-security check fails on both main and a factory PR; the PR closes before main recovers, leaving no ledger record of its failure.

gold.summary: Catalog mutation can invalidate a shadowed retained policy and prevent the daemon from restarting.

findings.title: Deleting a model referenced by the file-backed policy prevents restart
findings.detail: remove() checks only persisted operator cells. The evals policy loaded from routing/policy.json can also reference runtime models, but deletion leaves those references intact. Factory subsequently calls readPolicy() against the reduced catalog during startup, which throws and prevents the daemon from starting. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {RuntimeCatalog} from "./src/router/runtime-catalog.ts"; import {validatePolicy} from "./src/router/policy.ts"; const models=[{id:"codex/experiment",provider:"codex",source:"runtime",supportedEfforts:[]}]; const policy={triage:{default:["codex/experiment"]}}; const store={routingCells:()=>[],writeRuntimeModel:()=>{},publishCatalog:()=>{}}; const cat
findings.failure_scenario: Add codex/experiment, write an evals policy cell naming it, restart to activate that policy, then delete the model when no operator cell references it. Deletion succeeds, routing loses the target, and the next daemon restart fails while loading routing/policy.json.

gold.summary: Retrying an unchanged run converts inherited model chains into explicit overrides.
Routing previews remain stale after quota or cooldown expiry without an event.
Clearing a default effort omits the field from PATCH and leaves the old value stored.
Catalog history disappears on reload and does not include changes made by another client.

findings.title: Prefill retry chains using each role's actual routing complexity
findings.detail: The picker applies the original run's complexity to every role and submits those chains as explicit overrides. However, pipeline triage always routes with small, and deep-profile review routes with large. Opening this picker can therefore silently change untouched roles. Reproduction command: bun -e 'const s = await Bun.file("ui/components/RetryModels.tsx").text(); const e = s.match(/const groups = (.*);/)[1]; console.log(new Function("r", "role", "complexity", "return " + e)({effective:{triage:{small:{groups:["small/model"]},large:{groups:["large/model"]}}}}, "triage", "large"));' Output: [ "large/model" ]. The pipeline would select small/model.
findings.failure_scenario: A large run has no saved model overrides and routing has different triage.small and triage.large chains. Retrying after editing only implement submits triage.large as an override, replacing the triage.small chain that the pipeline actually uses.

findings.title: Clearing default effort does not clear the persisted value
findings.detail: An empty effort field omits effort from PATCH. RuntimeCatalog.patch merges the patch over the existing model, so the old effort survives despite a successful save. It also prevents removing that effort from supportedEfforts, because validation still sees the old default. Reproduction command: bun -e 'const s = await Bun.file("ui/components/CatalogForm.tsx").text(); const e = s.match(/\.\.\.\(f\.effort[^\n]+/)[0].slice(3).replace(/,$/, ""); const patch = new Function("f", "return " + e)({effort:""}); console.log({...{effort:"high"}, ...patch});' Output: { effort: "high" }.
findings.failure_scenario: Edit a runtime model with default effort high, erase Default effort and save. Reopening the editor shows high again, and routing continues to use it.

findings.title: Catalog history disappears when Setup is closed
findings.detail: Catalog history is populated only by local mutation callbacks into a component signal. Navigating away or reloading erases it, and catalog changes received through SSE never enter it. This does not provide the requested recent catalog changes alongside routing history.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or delete a runtime model, navigate to Models, then return to Setup. Catalog history is empty. Changes made by another operator are also absent despite the catalog updating over SSE.

gold.summary: Digest actions are derived from stale records instead of current unanswered and review state.
A historical failed review hides a later approval in MCP status.

findings.title: Stale approvals permanently hide PRs that need another review
findings.detail: review.approved removes the PR from the digest, but a subsequent head change invalidates the approval without generating another run.pr_opened or review.round_delivered event. The digest consequently reports no review needed even though the recorded approval is stale. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; import {digestCommand} from "./src/cli/digest.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const repo=s.upsertRepo({slug:"o/r",kind:"github",url:null,localPath:null,defaultBranch:"main",mergePolicy:"pr"}); const r=s.createRun(repo,{repo:"o/r",prompt:"work"}); const url="https://github.com/o/r/pull/1"; s.updateRun(r.id,{status:"succeeded",prUrl:url}); s.observePrHead(
findings.failure_scenario: A PR is approved, then someone pushes another commit outside a factory review round. A new session sees zero PRs awaiting review.

findings.title: Answered questions remain listed as needing user attention
findings.detail: Answering a question and returning to running emits none of the listed clearing events. The digest therefore continues presenting the answered question until the run finishes. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; import {digestCommand} from "./src/cli/digest.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const repo=s.upsertRepo({slug:"o/r",kind:"github",url:null,localPath:null,defaultBranch:"main",mergePolicy:"pr"}); const r=s.createRun(repo,{repo:"o/r",prompt:"work"}); const q=s.askQuestion(r.id,"Which option?"); s.answerQuestion(q.id,"A","human"); s.updateRun(r.id,{status:"running"}); await digestCommand([],{}, {api:async()=>s.readFeed({limit:1000}),print:console.log
findings.failure_scenario: A human answers an outstanding question without acknowledging that consumer's feed cursor; the run resumes and a later session digest asks for attention on the already answered question.

findings.title: Externally merged PRs remain in blocked lands
findings.detail: The blocked-land group ignores pr.merged and run.merged. An external merge does not transition the historical blocked entry to landed, so the digest retains an obsolete blocker. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { digestCommand } from "./src/cli/digest.ts"; import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; const url="https://github.com/o/r/pull/1"; const items=[{id:1,kind:"land.blocked",runId:"r",data:{url},title:"Blocked",summary:"CI failed"},{id:2,kind:"pr.merged",runId:"r",data:{url},title:"Merged",summary:"Merged externally"}]; const lines=[]; await digestCommand([], {}, {api:async()=>({items,nextAfter:2,pruned:false}),print:s=>lines.push(s)}); console.log(lines.join("\n")); assert.equa
findings.failure_scenario: Landing fails on CI; a maintainer fixes and merges the PR manually. Every subsequent unacknowledged digest still lists the old CI failure as a blocked land.

findings.title: Starting a review round does not clear the pending review request
findings.detail: review.round_started is ignored, leaving the original PR-opened item counted as awaiting review while the factory is applying the submitted findings. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { digestCommand } from "./src/cli/digest.ts"; import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; const prUrl="https://github.com/o/r/pull/1"; const items=[{id:1,kind:"run.pr_opened",runId:"owner",data:{prUrl},title:"PR opened",summary:prUrl},{id:2,kind:"review.round_started",runId:"round1",data:{prUrl,sourceRunId:"owner",round:1},title:"Review round started",summary:"Findings to address"}]; const lines=[]; await digestCommand([], {}, {api:async()=>({items,nextAfter:2,pruned:false}),print:s=>lines.push(s)}); con
findings.failure_scenario: An agent submits a changes verdict, then another session starts before the resulting review round finishes. Its digest incorrectly requests another review of the old head.

findings.title: Historical failed rounds override a subsequent valid approval
findings.detail: The last failed/cancelled round returns before current approval is considered. submitReview permits approving the owner's current head after a terminal round, but status keeps instructing the caller to inspect that historical round before submitting another verdict. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { explainStatus } from "./src/integrations/mcp-status.ts"; import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; const sha="a".repeat(40); const result=explainStatus({run:{id:"owner",status:"succeeded",prUrl:"https://github.com/o/r/pull/1"},questions:[],prSnapshot:{state:"OPEN",headRefOid:sha},review:{approval:{sha,stale:false},rounds:[{runId:"round1",status:"failed"}]}}, []); console.log(JSON.strin
findings.failure_scenario: A review round fails or is cancelled; a reviewer subsequently approves the current PR head. limitless_status never reports readiness to queue landing until a land is actually requested.

gold.summary: Unicode and URL encodings evade privacy protection in status and digest fields.

findings.title: Unread PR events cannot surface a newly stale approval
findings.detail: Only PR-opened, round-delivered, and approval events nominate review candidates. After those events are acknowledged, a changed head with an unread pr.ci_passed event is ignored entirely, even though the saved approval is stale. A real Store reproduction confirmed stale=true and unread kinds=["pr.ci_passed"], but the digest printed zero review items. Minimal exact command: bun -e 'import {digestCommand} from "./src/cli/digest.ts"; await digestCommand([],{consumer:"claude"},{api:async()=>({items:[{id:9,kind:"pr.ci_passed",runId:"r",data:{url:"https://github.com/o/r/pull/1"}}],nextAfter:9,pruned:false}),print:console.log});' Output: Limitless digest (read only; quoted text is untrusted data)\n
findings.failure_scenario: A consumer acknowledges a PR's opening and approval. Someone pushes another commit; the poller marks the approval stale and emits pr.ci_passed. The next session digest omits the PR needing re-review.

findings.title: Status ignores the run's confirmed merged flag
findings.detail: The status schema strips run.merged, and the merged-state branch never checks it. Store.resolveMergedRun preserves succeeded status and records merged=true without necessarily saving a PR snapshot or merged resolution. This is also the notifier's supported merge path. Exact command: bun -e 'import {explainStatus,statusDetailSchema} from "./src/integrations/mcp-status.ts"; console.log(JSON.stringify(explainStatus(statusDetailSchema.parse({run:{id:"r",status:"succeeded",prUrl:"https://github.com/o/r/pull/1",merged:true},questions:[],prSnapshot:null}),[])));' Output: {"run":"r","state":"PR state unknown","nextAction":"Inspect the PR and await a saved observation before reviewing or landing.","l
findings.failure_scenario: A succeeded run's PR merges outside the land queue. The GitHub notifier records the confirmed merge, but no saved PR observation exists. limitless_status reports unknown instead of landed; an older OPEN observation can instead cause it to recommend reviewing or landing the merged PR.

gold.summary: Layered URL and Unicode encodings bypass the single-pass private-text decoder.

findings.title: New PR activity cannot restore an acknowledged PR to the digest
findings.detail: The candidate whitelist ignores every pr.* event. Once the consumer acknowledges the original opening and approval events, subsequent GitHub activity never causes the digest to inspect that PR's current state, even when its approval has become stale. Reproduction command: LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR=/private/tmp/lr-3EbkhV/claude-501 bun -e 'import { digestCommand } from "./src/cli/digest.ts"; const prUrl="https://github.com/o/r/pull/1"; const items=[{id:9,kind:"pr.ci_passed",runId:"r1",data:{url:prUrl},title:"PR updated",summary:"CI passed at new head"}]; const detail={run:{id:"r1",status:"succeeded",prUrl},questions:[],prSnapshot:{state:"OPEN",headRefOid:"b".repeat(40)},review:{approval:{sha:"a".r
findings.failure_scenario: A consumer acknowledges a PR's approval, someone pushes a new head, and the poller emits pr.ci_passed for that head. The approval is stale, but the next session digest omits the PR.

findings.title: Active review rounds are incorrectly advertised as awaiting review
findings.detail: The actionable predicate checks approval and landing state but ignores review.rounds. Requesting changes invalidates the approval and starts a round, so an unread opening event continues to advertise the old head for review while changes are running. Reproduction command: LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR=/private/tmp/lr-3EbkhV/claude-501 TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-3EbkhV/claude-501 bun -e 'import { digestCommand } from "./src/cli/digest.ts"; const prUrl="https://github.com/o/r/pull/1"; const detail={run:{id:"r1",status:"succeeded",prUrl},questions:[],prSnapshot:{state:"OPEN",headRefOid:"a".repeat(40)},review:{approval:null,rounds:[{runId:"round1",status:"running",createdAt:2}]}}; const items=[{id:1,kind:"ru
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer requests changes without acknowledging the original PR event. A fresh session sees that PR as awaiting review while its changes round is still queued or running.

findings.title: Unreadable privacy policy allows mutations but discards their results
findings.detail: When loadOutputPrivacy returns null, the handler executes the tool before replacing its result with a generic message. It also returns success rather than an MCP error. For limitless_create_run this queues work but hides the generated run ID, preventing the caller from following the run or reliably determining whether a retry would duplicate it. Review and land similarly lose their mutation receipts.
findings.failure_scenario: private-strings.txt is unreadable or contains invalid UTF-8 and an agent calls limitless_create_run. The backend creates a run, but the successful MCP response contains only 'Tool output withheld; privacy policy unavailable.'

gold.summary: Smoke invocations do not honor the configured model-origin exclusions.

findings.title: Filter excluded verifiers before selecting from a panel list
findings.detail: The engine resolves every listed verifier and passes them to pickVerifier without filtering origins. pickVerifier can select an excluded model, after which the router receives an `only` constraint and rejects it. The panel fails even when another listed, independent verifier is allowed and available.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure exclude_origins=["CN"] and a panel verifier list with a CN model first and an allowed US model second. Neither verifier raised the finding and both have independent vendors. pickVerifier chooses the CN model; routing rejects it without considering the US verifier.

findings.title: Preserve origin exclusion reasons when chat routing exhausts candidates
findings.detail: The concierge discards RouteDecision.skipped and uses only candidates. When exclusions leave no chat candidate, it throws `No model available for chat`, or an earlier generic model failure, without the required origin exclusion reason. The new diagnostic handling in RunContext does not cover this invocation path.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure exclude_origins=["CN"] with a chat policy whose allowed providers are exhausted and whose remaining model is CN-origin. The router correctly excludes it, but the chat invocation fails with a generic message that omits `origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)`.

gold.summary: Queued chat dispatch uses a target whose origin became excluded after selection.
Queued eval dispatch does not revalidate origin eligibility after catalog changes.

findings.title: Recheck exclusions after waiting for chat capacity
findings.detail: The concierge retains the target returned by route() across acquire() and preflight() awaits. RuntimeCatalog.patch() can change that model's origin or baseOrigin and invalidate routing during either wait, but the concierge never observes that invalidation before dispatching the retained target. Consequently, an excluded model can still receive a chat prompt. RunContext.invoke() already checks routing revisions across these waits.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure exclude_origins=["CN"], select an allowed runtime model for chat, and keep its provider slot occupied. While the concierge waits, PATCH that model's origin and baseOrigin to CN. Release the slot: the concierge invokes the previously captured target despite its current exclusion.

findings.title: Preserve exclusion reasons when remaining verifiers cannot verify
findings.detail: Exclusion reasons are reported only when filtering empties the roster. If allowed entries remain but all raised the current candidate, pickVerifier() throws its generic independence error and discards the exclusion reasons. Exclusions can therefore remove the only usable verifier without the required origin-excluded reason appearing in the failure or run log.
findings.failure_scenario: Finder alpha raises a candidate. The verifier roster is [alpha, delta], where alpha is allowed and delta has excluded CN origin. Filtering leaves alpha, then pickVerifier() fails with 'raised a candidate it would check' and never reports 'origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)'.

gold.summary: The isolated post-check status still inspects populated submodules with their own git directories, so a submodule that points at the land clone's admin directory runs a clean filter from the clone's configuration, which the request says never applies after the checks.

findings.title: Submodule status escapes the isolated repository configuration
findings.detail: Git status recursively inspects populated submodules using their own Git directories. A check can redirect a submodule's .git file to the clone's admin directory and plant filter.attack.clean in the clone config. safe_git now enumerates filter keys only from the isolated repository, so the recursive status executes that clone-configured filter. The eventual dirty-tree refusal happens after execution. Full-script reproduction command: python3 "$TMPDIR/land-review-submodule.py". Output: "land exit: 1", "land stderr: Worktree differs from landing commit; refusing to land", "clone config command executed: True", followed by "AssertionError: post-check status executed the clone filter".
findings.failure_scenario: A landing commit contains a populated submodule and a filter-selected tracked file. During checks, code plants a clean-filter command in the clone config and redirects the submodule's .git file to the clone admin directory. Post-check status executes the command.

gold.summary: Removing a built-in model leaves persisted routing overrides unable to load at startup.
A runtime model attached to a retired provider prevents factory construction.
Historical run references prevent unrelated catalog mutations.

findings.title: Persisted references to the removed provider can prevent daemon startup
findings.detail: Removing the catalog entry leaves startup validation unchanged. RuntimePolicy rejects a persisted routing preference naming the removed provider; persisted routing cells and runtime models have similar rejection paths. Consequently, an existing database can prevent the daemon from starting, making historical records inaccessible. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { Store } from "./src/db/store.ts"; import { RuntimePolicy } from "./src/router/runtime-policy.ts"; import { MODELS, PROVIDERS } from "./src/router/catalog.ts"; const baseline = await Bun.file("test/fixtures/routing-identity.json").json(); const retired = baseline.snapshot.providers.find((id) => !PROVIDERS.some((p) => p.id === id
findings.failure_scenario: Before upgrading, an operator saved a routing preference containing the machine-named provider. After upgrading, Factory construction reaches RuntimePolicy and throws instead of starting.

findings.title: A valid IPv6 SSH destination crashes remote management
findings.detail: The new origin construction interpolates an SSH host directly into a URL. A bare IPv6 address is valid for SSH but requires brackets in an HTTP URL, so all local actions throw before issuing SSH commands. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { manageLocal } from "./src/cli/local.ts"; const calls = []; try { const report = await manageLocal("status", { remoteHost: "2001:db8::10", command: async (args) => { calls.push(args); return { exitCode: 0, stdout: "", stderr: "" }; }, probe: async () => true }); console.log(JSON.stringify(report)); } catch (error) { console.log(String(error)); console.log(`SSH calls: ${calls.length}`); process.exitCode = 1; }'. Output: TypeError: Invalid URL; SSH calls:
findings.failure_scenario: [local].remote_host is "2001:db8::10" and the remote unit is already installed. local status, up and down fail with Invalid URL before reaching the host.

gold.summary: Unavailable-target diagnostics expose registered credentials in routing API and Setup output.

findings.title: Restoring a retired model can persist a policy that prevents startup
findings.detail: The edit validator filters references against the old catalog, so references to the model being added are discarded before validation against the proposed catalog. Persisted operator cells are also absent from the filtered operator layer. Adding that model with incompatible efforts succeeds, but RuntimePolicy validates the resurrected reference on restart and throws. Reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-catalog.ts". Output: 'ADD accepted and persisted: [ "codex/restored" ]', followed by 'RESTART failed: Error: triage.default' and 'Unsupported effort "high" for codex/restored; supported: none'.
findings.failure_scenario: SQLite contains triage.default = ["codex/restored@high"], while codex/restored is absent. Add a runtime model with that id supporting only none, then restart the daemon.

findings.title: Historical evals containing the removed model cannot resume
findings.detail: The new compatibility test explicitly expects HTTP 400 when resuming a historical eval. EvalRunner.resume resubmits the stored request through strict current-catalog validation, which rejects the removed model and prevents the entire eval from continuing, including trials targeting available models. Removing the built-in model introduces this failure for previously valid stored requests and does not satisfy the requirement that pre-change records still resume.
findings.failure_scenario: An interrupted pre-change eval stores a request containing the machine-named model and an available Codex model. After upgrading, POST /api/evals/:id/resume returns 400 with unknown model ID.

gold.summary: Raw process output is cut before gate credential redaction can match a boundary-spanning secret.

findings.title: Redaction happens after the process runner has already truncated output
findings.detail: runConfined returns streams already truncated to 64,000 characters by runProcess. A credential crossing that boundary cannot match redactCredentials. Removing terminal formatting then brings its surviving suffix into the final 6,000-character result, which consumers store and forward. A targeted `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-5iTEAw/claude-501 TMP=$TMPDIR TEMP=$TMPDIR bun -e` probe invoking runGates with the input described below returned output `ndary-credential-409` and failed with `error: Credential suffix leaked after upstream tail truncation`.
findings.failure_scenario: Register `synthetic-upstream-boundary-credential-409`, then have a gate print that value followed by 15,995 ANSI reset sequences (`\u001b[0m`). The 64,000-character process tail splits the credential; stripping those sequences leaves `ndary-credential-409` unredacted in GateResult.output.

gold.summary: JSON escaping lets ordinary logged credentials evade literal gate-output redaction.
Line callbacks store pieces of multiline credentials in failure excerpts.

findings.title: Multiline credentials survive in stored failure excerpts
findings.detail:
Redaction receives individual lines, so it cannot match a registered credential containing a newline. FailureExcerpts rejoins those lines and returns the credential unchanged. A direct runGates probe confirmed that output was redacted while failures retained the complete credential. Minimal reproduction command: bun -e 'import { registerCredential } from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import { extractFailures } from "./src/gates/failures.ts"; registerCredential("MULTILINE_REVIEW_TOKEN", "secret-part-one
secret-part-two"); console.log(extractFailures("error: secret-part-one
secret-part-two
(fail) assertion"));'. Output: error: secret-part-one
secret-part-two
(fail) assertion, with actual newlines
findings.failure_scenario: A failing check prints a registered multiline credential, such as a private key, followed by a failure result. The returned failures field contains the credential and is persisted in gate artifacts and state.

findings.title: Whole-state redaction corrupts resume control fields
findings.detail: redactGateData rewrites every string in live RunState, including phase, rather than only gate diagnostics. redactCredentials replaces short credentials when the entire string matches. Command: bun -e 'import { registerCredential } from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import { redactGateData } from "./src/gates/output.ts"; registerCredential("RESUME_REVIEW_TOKEN", "loop"); console.log(JSON.stringify(redactGateData({ flow: "build", phase: "loop", round: 2 })));'. gold.summary: Arbitrary assertion text mentioning a timeout is classified as a transient CI failure.
Retry eligibility ignores security failures outside the selected error line.
A paused PR is not inspected again when main recovers without another PR change.
An accepted rerun with a lost response is never reconciled to its later result.

findings.title: Resume suppressed PR failures when main recovers
findings.detail: Classification returns successfully after suppressing a failure because main is red, clearing ciPending. Subsequent classification requires a change to the PR's ciKey. Main recovering does not change that key, so an unchanged failed PR remains suppressed indefinitely, without a rerun or ci.needs_fix.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR and main both have a failing test check. The first poll emits ci.main_red and clears pending inspection. Main then passes after a fix or rerun, while the PR's failed check remains unchanged. Later polls never reconsider that PR failure.

findings.title: Reconcile reruns whose POST response was lost
findings.detail: The reconciliation loop only handles outcome rerunning. A crash or lost response after GitHub accepts the POST leaves rerun_requested, which is never inspected for later-attempt evidence. A subsequent successful rollup completes inspection without recording the flake; a failed observation instead marks it failed_again without establishing the rerun result. The isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probe.ts"` produced `{"done":true,"outcome":"rerun_requested","attemptEvidenceFetched":false}` and `FAIL: confirmed same-SHA rerun pass was not recorded`.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a rerun, but its response is lost or the daemon exits before finishCiFailure sets rerunning. After restart, attempt 2 passes at the same SHA. The ledger remains rerun_requested permanently instead of recording failed_then_passed.

findings.title: Resume suppressed PR failures when main recovers
findings.detail: Main-red suppression completes the inspection and clears ciPending. Subsequent polls skip classification while the PR's GraphQL state remains unchanged, so recovery of main never resumes the PR reaction. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` reproduced: `main recovered, unchanged PR: {"reruns":0,"needsFix":0,"mainReads":1,"ciPending":false}`.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR job times out while the same check fails on main. Main subsequently becomes green, but the PR remains red at the same SHA. The PR receives neither its transient rerun nor ci.needs_fix, indefinitely.

findings.title: Reconcile rerun requests with ambiguous responses
findings.detail: Reconciliation excludes rerun_requested rows. If GitHub accepts the POST but its response is lost, the persisted claim remains rerun_requested. A subsequent success clears inspection without recording the flake; a still-red observation can instead label it failed_again without inspecting the rerun. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` reproduced: `accepted rerun whose response was lost, then same-SHA pass: {"outcome":"rerun_requested","runLookups":0,"ciPending":false}`.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a job rerun, the connection resets before the 201 response arrives, and that rerun passes at the original SHA. The ledger never records failed_then_passed, including after restart.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: Unaccepted rerun requests remain pending forever
findings.detail: A 429, network failure before submission, or crash between claiming and posting leaves outcome rerun_requested. When GitHub never creates another attempt, reconciliation always continues here, and the pending prior record suppresses ci.needs_fix indefinitely. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: after 100 reconciliation polls {"complete":false,"posts":1,"outcome":"rerun_requested","needsFix":0}; Expected: true, Received: false.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub rejects the rerun with HTTP 429 and run_attempt remains 1, or the daemon crashes after claiming but before sending the POST.

findings.title: Lagging check data reports a confirmed passing rerun as needing a fix
findings.detail: Successful reconciliation adds only the new job ID to resolved. If the check-runs endpoint still returns the original failed job, that ID is not skipped. The prior failed_then_passed record prevents another rerun but falls through to needsFix, producing contradictory ledger and feed results. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: successful rerun with lagging checks {"outcome":"failed_then_passed","feed":["ci.needs_fix"]}; Expected: false, Received: true.
findings.failure_scenario: A pending inspection observes attempt 2 succeeding through the workflow jobs API while GraphQL and the commit check-runs endpoint still expose attempt 1's failure.

findings.title: Main-red suppression bypasses the failure ledger
findings.detail: The main-red branch continues before fetching job evidence, constructing the signature, or recording the failure. Consequently, these failures have no ledger record despite the requirement to record each failure signature, SHA, and outcome. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: main-red result {"ledgerRows":0,...}; Expected: 1, Received: 0.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory PR's non-security test job fails while the default branch is red on the same check; ci.main_red is emitted, but ci_failures remains empty.

findings.title: Rate-limited rerun requests remain pending forever
findings.detail: A rejected 429 response leaves the durable claim as rerun_requested. Subsequent inspections wait for run_attempt to increase, but GitHub never accepted the rerun, so neither a retry nor ci.needs_fix occurs. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced `{"name":"rate-limit-rejection","posts":1,"outcomes":["rerun_requested"],"needsFix":0,"error":"Error: CI job rerun was not confirmed"}` after four inspections.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub rejects the rerun POST with HTTP 429; the workflow remains at its original attempt across subsequent polls and restarts.

findings.title: One CI inspection failure starves later PR observations
findings.detail: Classifier exceptions escape record and terminate the repository's observation loop. Because ciPending remains persisted, the same PR repeats the failure every poll and prevents later PRs from recording CI, review, closure, or merge observations. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-poller-review.ts"` across three polls saved only `https://github.com/o/r/pull/1`; each poll logged `Incomplete CI inspection: commits/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa/check-runs?filter=latest&per_page=100&page=1 (404)`.
findings.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR repeatedly returns unavailable or malformed CI details while a later PR has valid GraphQL observations.

findings.title: Case-sensitive API URL validation rejects valid repositories
findings.detail: Repository registration preserves the user's slug casing, while GitHub returns canonical casing in check_run_url. This strict comparison rejects a legitimate job even though the preceding details_url comparison accepts case differences. The rerun reconciliation prefix check has the same problem. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` with stored `o/r` and returned `O/R` produced `{"name":"canonical-repo-case","posts":0,"outcomes":[],"needsFix":0,"error":"Error: Incomplete failing job"}`.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository is registered using lowercase owner/name, but GitHub's canonical owner or repository name contains uppercase characters.

findings.title: Test timeout classification excludes the requested diagnostic
findings.detail: Only three hardcoded diagnostic formats qualify. An actual failure line such as `error: smoke timed out after 30000ms` is classified as needs-fix despite matching the requested test timeout case. The added tests explicitly expect this exclusion. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced `{"name":"test-own-timeout","posts":0,"outcomes":["failed"],"needsFix":4,"error":""}`.
findings.failure_scenario: A test runner reports its own timeout as `error: smoke timed out after 30000ms` and the Actions job concludes failure.

findings.title: Main-branch status lookup depends on the PR's context types
findings.detail: The shared checks function fetches legacy commit statuses only when the PR snapshot contains StatusContext entries or is truncated. Consequently, a failing main status is invisible when the PR exposes the same check through CheckRun. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` with a failing main status named test produced `{"name":"main-red-legacy-status","posts":1,"mainStatusReads":0,"outcomes":["rerunning"],"needsFix":0,"error":""}`.
findings.failure_scenario: Main reports a failing legacy commit status named test, while the factory PR reports test through the Checks API.

gold.summary: Catalog mutation can invalidate a shadowed retained policy and prevent the daemon from restarting.

findings.title: Clear stale backend rejection when replacing a runtime model
findings.detail: Catalog updates replace the router definition but retain ProviderTracker.modelBlocks, which are keyed only by catalog ID. A rejection of the old backend therefore blocks the replacement backend for up to 24 hours. Deleting and re-adding the ID also retains the block. Check: `bun "$TMPDIR/catalog-review.ts" block` printed `{"candidates":[],"skipped":[{"modelId":"codex/experiment","reason":"codex: model rejected: old-build is not available"}]}` and failed with `AssertionError: patched new backend must not inherit old backend rejection` (`0 !== 1`).
findings.failure_scenario: A runtime model targeting old-build receives a model rejection. The operator patches its backend to an available new-build and explicitly routes to it. Routing still skips it because of old-build's rejection.

findings.title: Prevent older probes from overwriting newer discovery results
findings.detail: Each probe unconditionally records its response without request ordering or a generation check. Concurrent probes can finish out of order, persisting an obsolete served set and making the router reject a currently served model. Provider enable operations can start probes alongside scheduled probes. Check: `bun "$TMPDIR/catalog-review.ts" ordering` printed `{"served":["retired-build"],"candidates":[],"skipped":[{"modelId":"omlx/qwen-flash","reason":"not served by omlx"}]}` and failed with `AssertionError: late older probe must not overwrite newer served list` (`0 !== 1`).
findings.failure_scenario: An older probe captures the previous backend list. A second probe observes the replacement model and completes first. The older response then arrives and replaces the current discovery result, so routing skips the replacement until another successful probe.

findings.detail: Catalog history renders only the component-local session signal, populated by this component's mutation callbacks. Navigating away or refreshing erases all entries. findings.title: Historical landing blocks override closed and resolved states
findings.detail: The blocked-land branch runs before checks for resolved runs and closed PRs. Because blocked entries persist, status continues recommending another landing request after the work has been resolved. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-probes.ts". For a resolved run with a CLOSED PR, output includes "state":"Landing blocked" and "nextAction":"Inspect the land reason, resolve the blocker, then request limitless_land again." The landing API rejects closed PRs.
findings.failure_scenario: Landing blocks, the PR is closed, and the run is resolved as pr_closed. limitless_status still instructs the agent to queue landing again.

findings.title: Honor the run's persisted merge flag
findings.detail: The status schema strips run.merged, and the landed condition never checks it. Existing delivery paths persist merged=true without recording a merged PR snapshot or land entry, so status can describe a confirmed merge as unknown or awaiting review. Boundary command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-boundaries.ts". Output: FAIL persisted merged run: expected "Landed", got "PR state unknown".
findings.failure_scenario: Delivery successfully merges under the auto policy and stores run.merged=true; GitHub polling is disabled or has not saved a merged observation, and there is no land entry.

findings.title: Let a closed PR supersede a historical landing blocker
findings.detail: The blocked-land branch runs before the CLOSED PR check. After someone closes a blocked PR, status still instructs the agent to resolve the blocker and request limitless_land again, although the landing API rejects closed PRs. Boundary command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-boundaries.ts". Output: FAIL closed PR with historical blocked land: expected "PR closed", got "Landing blocked".
findings.failure_scenario: A land blocks on CI, then the PR is closed without merging and its CLOSED observation is saved.

findings.failure_scenario: The consumer has not acknowledged the original PR-opened event, and a changes verdict has created a queued or running review round on that PR.

findings.title: Revalidate chat routing after asynchronous slot waits
findings.detail: Chat checks origins only when selecting the initial target. It then awaits tracker.acquire() and tracker.preflight() without observing router.policyRevision or checking the current catalog again. RuntimeCatalog.patch() permits changing origin/baseOrigin and invalidates routing, but this pending chat still invokes its saved target. Thus a model currently marked excluded can receive chat content. RunContext handles routing invalidation after these waits; Concierge needs equivalent protection.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure exclude_origins=["CN"], route chat to an allowed runtime model, and occupy its provider slot. While chat waits, patch that model's origin/baseOrigin to CN. Release the slot: the pending chat invokes the saved target even though a fresh route excludes it.

findings.title: Late config injection targets the isolated repository
findings.detail: The fake gh process inherits GIT_COMMON_DIR pointing at the isolated repository. Passing --git-dir for the clone does not override that variable, so these config commands modify the isolated repository instead of the clone. A two-repository probe confirmed the setting was absent from the clone and present in the isolated repository. Consequently, the passing pre-push:clean-filter test does not exercise the explicitly requested late clone-config injection.

findings.detail: The overlap uses literal credential lengths, although redactCredentials also recognizes longer JSON-escaped variants. Terminal-control stripping changes with chunk boundaries and loses state at the hold limit.

findings.title: Overlapping matches make the raw carry buffer unbounded
findings.detail: With the registered credential `aaaaaaaa`, every overlapping occurrence moves `cut` backwards until it reaches zero. Repeated chunks of `a` therefore remain entirely in `pending`, bypassing tailLimit and repeatedly rescanning accumulated output. A mocked-pipe reproduction retained all 48,000 raw characters across three writes despite tailLimit 100; registering that entire string immediately before EOF produced stdout `[redacted]` with truncated false. Sustained gate output can exhaust daemon memory and CPU.
findings.failure_scenario: Register `aaaaaaaa`, then run a gate continuously emitting `a` without newlines. The daemon accumulates the complete raw stream instead of retaining a bounded suffix.

findings.title: Redaction can corrupt the trusted sandbox startup marker
findings.detail: runSandboxed recognizes its `limitless-started-<uuid>` handshake through onStdoutLine, which now receives redacted text. Registering `limitless-started-` as a credential changes that handshake before comparison. A direct runSandboxed reproduction using `/usr/bin/true`, redactOutput true and an identity confinement backend returned `Error: Write confinement payload did not start: 0`, although the payload succeeded.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured credential contains the value `limitless-started-` (or another matching substring of the startup marker). Every gate reports a confinement startup failure regardless of its actual exit status.
